summary: External IP 203.0.113.47 made repeated failed SSH logins against multiple accounts on internet-facing production server web-prod-02, then successfully authenticated as the 'deploy' service account from a source not in its expected login list. Confidence is held below certain because no threat intel on the source IP and no post-login activity data were provided.

key_evidence.claim: Six failed SSH password attempts from 203.0.113.47 within ~3 minutes, including guesses against non-existent users 'admin' and 'root'
The same source IP then successfully authenticated as user 'deploy' via password
The 'deploy' account is a CI/CD service account not expected to log in interactively, and 203.0.113.47 is not in its expected login sources
The affected host is a high-criticality, internet-facing production web server
The same source IP triggered prior brute-force and non-existent-user alerts on this host in the preceding 20 minutes

attack_techniques.name: Brute Force
attack_techniques.justification: Mapped by the alert itself (alert.rule.mitre) and consistent with the repeated failed logins across multiple usernames in alert.previous_output

evidence_gaps: No threat intel reputation data for source IP 203.0.113.47
No post-login activity (commands, sessions, outbound connections) for the successful 'deploy' login
Unknown whether the 'deploy' account password was recently rotated or is shared
No geolocation or ASN information for the source IP
recommended_actions: Review sshd and shell history on web-prod-02 for activity by 'deploy' after 2026-07-21T03:17:41Z
Consider resetting the 'deploy' account credential and rotating any secrets it can access
Consider blocking or rate-limiting 203.0.113.47 at the perimeter pending investigation
Check other internet-facing hosts for authentication attempts from 203.0.113.47
Evaluate enforcing key-based authentication for service accounts on this host
escalation_reason: Likely successful credential-access attack on a high-criticality internet-facing production server; a service account shows an authenticated session from an unexpected external source.
